_comment: Copy this beside where you want build-state.json to live, then edit. Every value here is a placeholder. Provider names resolve to workspace-local ids at build time; ids are never hardcoded, because a function id means nothing in another workspace. A provider type of 'none' means NO PROVIDER IS AVAILABLE for that leg — never use it to switch off a field the installer is not interested in. What gets attempted is decided per record by the skip flags at run time, so build every leg a provider can reach. An http leg must name app_account — the Clay HTTP API account holding that provider's key. No credential ever goes in this file. A leg's `skip` names the caller opt-out that switches it off; omit `skip` for an ENABLING lookup that should run only when a leg downstream requires its field.
_comment_config_home: OPTIONAL. Only set this when this workspace's Clay credential is deliberately separate from your default `clay login`. Omit it to use the ambient login.
_comment_tuning: All three below are optional and shown at their defaults.

legs._comment: An ENABLING lookup that can also be requested. It carries `want` (opt-IN, default off) rather than `skip` (opt-out, default on), because it exists for the legs after it rather than for its own sake — so it fires whenever something downstream requires a domain, and otherwise only when a caller asks with want_company_domain. Opt-out polarity would fire it on every record where the domain is missing, adding cost nobody asked for.
A flat-rate provider that finds the pivot from name + company. This is the valuable shape: it lands BEFORE the pivot and unlocks every leg that needs a profile URL.
A vendor with a native Clay action. Resolve by the (actionPackageId, actionKey) PAIR — a key alone can collide across packages.

provider.actionPackageId: <its package id from the same row>

legs._comment: Flat-rate email, keyed off the pivot. `requires` is what makes this SKIP rather than fire and die when the pivot was never found.
A GET provider: query parameters rather than a JSON body.

provider.app_account: <your other Clay HTTP API account name>

legs._note: A GET provider: query parameters rather than a JSON body. Note the direction — the KEY is the provider's own parameter name (theirs, from their spec) and the VALUE is our record field. They are often spelled differently and that is fine.

legs._comment: The credit-billed fallback. It runs only when every flat-rate leg above came back empty, which is the one boundary where cost-ascending ordering actually saves money.

Phone is the dearest field on the platform — and the leg is still built. It fires only on a record that wants a phone and whose free lookup missed, and skip_phone stops it entirely. Leaving it out of the graph to save money would mean a rebuild the first time somebody wants a phone number.
Verification reports, it never rewrites. The address is always emitted; the verdict decides whether contact_email_verified_only is populated.

_comment_enabler: Every field a provider can reach gets a leg, and every leg carries a skip flag so a caller can both request and suppress it per record. A leg still fires when a downstream leg REQUIRES its field, flag or no flag — otherwise the downstream leg could never run. Omit `skip` entirely only for a field nobody should ever be able to request.
